summary: Create a Run and bind it as this profile's current Run
usage: corral orchestration run-create [--objective VALUE] [--request-id VALUE] [--help] [--json] [--timeout-ms VALUE] [--socket VALUE] [--instance VALUE]
notes: Records are Run (run_<12 hex>), Task (task_<12 hex>) and Dispatch (ctx_<12 hex>), stored as one JSON document under <userData>/runtime/orchestration/state.json. One mutation is one atomic rename, so a task, its attempt and any dependents promoted by the same call commit together or not at all. Durability is the profile's existing promise: process-crash safe, not power-loss safe (no directory fsync, no F_FULLFSYNC). A document that is damaged, foreign or internally inconsistent is storage_corrupt and is never rewritten, truncated or reinitialized; an absent one is simply a new profile.

The current Run is bound per profile, not per calling terminal. --run <id> overrides it for one call without rebinding it. With neither, commands that need a Run fail run_required before any effect and before any receipt is written, and resources.recovery names run-create/run-use.

Task status is pending|ready|dispatched|completed|failed|blocked; Dispatch status is dispatched|completed|failed|unknown. failed means an observed failure only: an absent pane, a replaced PTY, a changed backend generation and an unreachable backend are never turned into failed, and nothing is retried automatically.

Every mutation accepts --request-id r1.<13-digit Unix milliseconds>.<UUID> and mints one when it is omitted, sharing the profile's existing 24-hour receipt store. A replayed id returns the first result with replayed true, the same id with different input is request_conflict, and a receipt that is still pending is outcome_unknown and is never re-executed.
This command group starts nothing and sends nothing to any pane. Dispatch records which pane an attempt is bound to; launching the worker, its messages and its completion are LIFE-410.
run-create always rebinds the current Run to the Run it created.

Reconcile re-observes every open attempt before each orchestration command, once when the runtime starts, and again on dispatch-show for an attempt that is still open: the same generation alive keeps the attempt dispatched and reports terminal.live true; an absent pane, a replaced PTY or a changed backend generation settles it unknown with reason pane_gone|pty_replaced|epoch_changed and leaves the Task dispatched so it can be dispatched again; an unreachable backend records nothing at all and reports observed false with terminal.live unknown. The observation has its own budget - 2000 ms, and never more than half of the time the caller has left - so a backend that never answers cannot hold a read command open; exceeding it is the same as could not look. A reconcile result is stored by a read command - that record stands whether the read then succeeds or fails - or by the mutation it travels with; a rejected mutation writes nothing at all. Only reconcile creates unknown, and it never creates failed.

The manual table is dispatched -> completed|failed, anything except completed -> blocked, and blocked -> ready|pending. ready -> dispatched belongs to the dispatch command alone, and completed is terminal. An open attempt additionally refuses -> blocked: settle it with completed|failed, or let reconcile close it once its pane is gone, so a live worker is never left with an attempt no command can end. Anything else is illegal_transition with the allowed set in resources.

For a request that passes validation the checks run in a fixed order and every rejection is effect-free: --expected-version mismatch is version_conflict, then an illegal transition is illegal_transition, then a --dispatch that is not the open attempt is stale_dispatch. Settling a Task that is already settled is therefore illegal_transition even when the caller names the attempt that settled it, while naming a superseded attempt of a still-open Task is stale_dispatch. Flag validation runs before all of them, so --status dispatched is illegal_transition whatever the other flags say.

Omitting --dispatch settles whichever attempt is open, which is how a human settles a Task whose attempt reconcile already marked unknown. blocked -> ready additionally requires every dependency completed; blocked -> pending is always available.

--result is stored only by --status completed|failed; giving it to any other transition is invalid_argument rather than a silently dropped value.

--to takes a terminal handle and is resolved by the terminal module's own three-layer check: a handle that does not verify is invalid_terminal, one from another runtime or backend generation or whose PTY is gone or replaced is stale_terminal, and a profile with no reachable backend is backend_unavailable. All three are effect-free.

The attempt stores the target identity (handle, runtimeId, epoch, ptyId, paneId) and a snapshot of the pane's managed agent taken at that moment, or null with agentAbsenceReason when the pane has none. The agent block is an observation made at dispatch time and is never refreshed: a pane dispatched while its provider was still launching keeps phase launching and resolvedModel null for the life of the record. Read the pane itself with terminal show for its current state. Nothing is sent to the pane and no agent is started.

A Task is startable when it is ready, or when its most recent attempt ended failed or unknown - that retry becomes attempt n+1. For an attempt that was still open when the call started the response's terminal block is the observation this call made (source observation), including the one that settles it unknown; for an attempt that was already settled the backend is not contacted at all and the block repeats the stored reconcile with live null and source record. The record's reconcile block is the last observation that changed something, with the runtime instance that recorded it. Repeating the call therefore leaves the stored document byte-identical.
